newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 87 in January.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 87 in January.

text.p: The U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose to 87.0 in January from 85.0 in December, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
"Strong labor demand suggests that the pace of job growth will be maintained at least through spring," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein.

In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising increased in six of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increase was in the Middle Atlantic region, up 30.6 percent. Other regional increases were the West North Central, up 7.7 percent, Pacific, up 5.8 percent and East North Central, up 4.9 percent.
Regional declines were in the Mountain, down 2.8 percent, South Atlantic, down 1.9 percent and New England, down 0.3 percent.

Goldstein said "there has been concern over the last two years that the economy might begin to weaken, and that layoffs might pick up. The data, however, have consistently shown no such developments."
